content:
Fixed `intervals.py`.

Root cause: the old code materialized every integer in every interval into a `set`, so it was O(total span) time/memory (catastrophic for huge ranges) and its `range(a, b)` yielded nothing for reversed pairs (`a >= b`), silently dropping data.

Fix: normalize by dropping non-positive-length pairs, sort by start, merge overlapping/touching intervals (`start <= cur_end`), and sum merged lengths. O(n log n) time, O(n) space, no point expansion.

Verified:
- `test_public.py` → PUBLIC_OK
- 10 targeted edge cases (reversed, negative, duplicated, nested, touching, empty, enormous ±10^12) pass
- 2000 randomized cases match a brute-force set reference
- 300k huge-range intervals in 0.087s; 1M touching unit intervals (would-be 10^6 expansion) in 0.138s

Working tree contains the updated `intervals.py`; no tests or metadata touched.
